task.description: Step 1 diagnosis for ISS-0480 (MAJOR): reproduce, root-cause, and determine remedy for the intermittent RowApprovalTest/PackUpdateMigrationTest failures. Do NOT implement a fix -- route to CODE-DESIGNER.

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 REGISTRY LOOKUP: ISS-0113 ('provisioned_tenant/0 sets Sandbox.mode(:auto) and never restores :manual') is the same MECHANISM, not a coincidental prior-art citation. This is NOT a recurrence of a fix that failed to hold -- ISS-0113 was never fixed for the general case; it was fixed only for 2 of 46 TenantFixture call sites (secrets_test.exs, webhooks_test.exs, per its resolution note), and this issue (ISS-0480) is exactly the previously-unconsidered SIDE EFFECT of that fix on two UNRELATED async:true files that don't call Sandbox.mode/2 at all. Recorded here so CODE-DESIGNER does not treat ISS-0113 as closed/irrelevant.

===== ROOT CAUSE, CONFIRMED BY SOURCE READ + REPRODUCTION =====

THE MECHANISM (traced through actual Ecto/DBConnection source, same technique ISS-0113's design doc section 9 used): `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(repo, mode)` -> `DBConnection.Ownership.Manager.handle_call({:mode, mode}, {caller, _}, state)` (deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex:169-172): when the requested mode differs from the pool's current mode, it calls `proxy_checkin_all_except(state, [], caller)` -- the except-list is the LITERAL EMPTY LIST. This unconditionally checks in EVERY currently-checked-out connection for EVERY process in the pool, not just the caller's, and not just processes that themselves call Sandbox.mode/2. This is documented at manager.ex and was already traced once before, in lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md section 9.1/9.4 -- but that design's own section 9.4 safety argument explicitly rests on the load-bearing (and self-flagged-as-fragile, 'OQ-5') premise that 'every other async:true file calling Sandbox.mode(:auto) collides with nothing because no OTHER async:true file also calls Sandbox.mode/2'. That premise addresses only the two-caller-both-flip-mode case (proven safe: whichever goes first has nothing to discard because the caller's own checkout hasn't happened yet at that point in provisioned_tenant!/1). It does NOT address a THIRD kind of process: an async:true test that checks out its connection in DataCase.setup/1 (test/support/data_case.ex:16, unconditional Sandbox.checkout for every test, async or not) and then does NOT itself call Sandbox.mode/2 at all -- RowApprovalTest and PackUpdateMigrationTest are exactly this third kind. Their connection is checked out for the whole test body, and is just as unconditionally discarded as anyone else's by the empty-except-list check-in, the FIRST time ANY concurrently-running async:true test calls Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto).

WHY THIS IS A GENUINE GAP, NOT A REPEAT OF ISS-0113's OWN QUESTION: ISS-0113's design doc explicitly scoped its own safety analysis to 'a FUTURE tranche converting a 3rd/4th file' -- i.e. a future file that ALSO calls Sandbox.mode(:auto). It never considered a file that never calls Sandbox.mode/2 at all but is simply an innocent bystander holding an open connection when someone else's mode flip fires. RowApprovalTest and PackUpdateMigrationTest are that bystander case, and they predate ISS-0423's 2-file conversion (both are empty-diff against main and were async:true before secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs were converted) -- so ISS-0423's conversion is what turned a previously-inert Sandbox.mode(:auto) call (inert because it only ran during the async:false/sync phase, per ExUnit's own scheduler -- see below) into one that now runs DURING the async phase, where RowApprovalTest/PackUpdateMigrationTest's connections are live.

WHY ExUnit'S SYNC/ASYNC PHASE SEPARATION DOES NOT SAVE THIS (checked directly, not assumed): read "C:\Program Files\Elixir\lib\ex_unit\lib\ex_unit\runner.ex" async_loop/4 (lines 104-138). It confirmed ExUnit really does run ALL async:true modules to completion (0 = map_size of `running` after draining) before EVER starting an async:false module -- so the ORIGINAL hypothesis in ISS-0480's own description (an async:false test's Sandbox.mode(:auto) call racing a still-running async:true test) is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE and is NOT the mechanism. The ~40+ async:false files calling Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) (audit_test.exs, migrations_test.exs, promotion_conflict_test.exs, identity_test.exs, etc. -- grepped directly, full list in this run's tool output) are irrelevant to this defect: by the time any of them runs, every async:true test (RowApprovalTest and PackUpdateMigrationTest included) has already finished and released its connection. The REAL culprits are the two ASYNC:TRUE files that call it -- test/letflow/secrets_test.exs and test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs (confirmed: `grep -rl "Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)" test | xargs -I{} grep -m1 'async:' {}` -- these are the only two async:true hits besides two files that only mention :auto in comments/moduledoc prose, not in executable code: test/letflow/api/authorization_ac9_test.exs and test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs, both confirmed by direct read to NOT call Sandbox.mode/2 despite the string match).

===== REPRODUCTION, WITH REAL MEASURED HIT RATE =====

Environment note (reported plainly, not swept under 'green run'): this host had FOUR orphaned `mix test --seed 1` erl.exe processes still live and connected to letflow_test when I started (Windows ISS-0107 recursion bug -- my own earlier attempts to run the suite in one blocking call got moved to background by the tool's 120s default timeout and their erl.exe processes outlived the shell wrapper; a subsequent 590s-timeout attempt suffered the identical fate, plus a stray post-kill child). All were verified via `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` (parent/cmdline) before killing, Postgres connection counts checked before/after via `pg_stat_activity`, and the mandated tenant_template cleanup re-run after each cleanup. This is disclosed because it produced a real, misleading 'too many connections' failure during one `mix ecto.create` attempt that is NOT evidence about ISS-0480's mechanism -- it was self-inflicted environment noise, corrected before the real reproduction runs below.

The project's full `mix test` run measured at ~7-10 minutes wall clock (config/test.exs default log level logs every SQL statement at :debug, producing ~685k lines matching the issue's own prior-run figure) -- this exceeds this tool's 600000ms (10 min) hard per-call cap for a single blocking foreground call, so I could not run the literal full suite to completion in one call without violating the 'no backgrounding a long-running op' rule. Per that rule's own intent (measure the real property under real conditions rather than a diluted proxy), I instead ran the full ASYNC-PHASE cohort together -- all 95 files declaring `async: true` (`grep -rl "async: true" test --include=*.exs`), which is the actual concurrency domain this defect lives in (both target files, both culprit files, and every other async:true file, all scheduled by ExUnit's real max_cases=32 concurrency, same pool_size=32 -- config/test.exs, System.schedulers_online()=16 on this host) -- each run bounded at 560s, well inside budget, and each preceded by fresh tenant_template cleanup and a verified-clean process/connection state.

MEASURED RESULTS, 4 consecutive runs, varying --seed (which reorders ExUnit's module scheduling and therefore perturbs the race window), all against the unmodified branch tip (no code changed):
  - seed 1: FAILED -- Letflow.RowApprovalTest "approving the same approver twice is idempotent" -- MatchError, `{0, nil}` (a Repo.update_all matching ZERO rows) where `assert :ok = RowApproval.approve(id, :finance)` expected `:ok`.
  - seed 2: PASSED -- 1754/1754, 0 failures.
  - seed 3: FAILED -- Letflow.RowApprovalTest "approving the same approver twice is idempotent" -- IDENTICAL failure signature to seed 1 (same test, same line, same `{0, nil}`).
  - seed 4: FAILED -- Letflow.RowApprovalTest "an unsupervised approver atom is rejected, not silently accepted" -- `RowApproval.get(id)` returned `{:error, :not_found}` right after the SAME test's own `create_instance!()` had just inserted that row -- this is the LITERAL failure shape ISS-0480's own description quotes for the ORIGINAL discovering run's OTHER RowApprovalTest failure ("finance then ops reaches :approved"), confirming this is the same intermittent defect, not a new one.

HIT RATE: 3 of 4 runs failed (75%), all three failures in Letflow.RowApprovalTest, three DIFFERENT individual tests within that one file each time (consistent with a race that can land on whichever test happens to be mid-flight at the moment the disruptive Sandbox.mode(:auto) call fires -- not a defect in one specific test). PackUpdateMigrationTest did NOT fail in any of my 4 runs -- stated plainly per the No Speculation directive: I could NOT reproduce PackUpdateMigrationTest's own fkey-constraint failure on this host in this session, despite 4 real attempts under real full-async-cohort concurrency. I do not treat this as clearing it -- see 'ONE DEFECT OR TWO' below -- but it is an honest gap in this run's evidence, not swept into 'presumed the same'.

CAUSAL TRACE FOR ONE CONCRETE FAILURE (seed 1's `{0,nil}` case), tied to real log timestamps (log saved at $TEMP/iss0480_async_run1.log on the diagnosing host, not committed -- ephemeral per this project's own convention for raw suite logs, matching ISS-0480's own description noting the original 684k-line logs were never committed either):
  - 12:44:53.272 -- `INSERT INTO "approvals" ... ["ff989f08-6045-4e86-b197-9d4ea7042570"]` (RowApprovalTest's create_instance!/0).
  - 12:44:53.275 -- `SELECT ... FROM "approvals" WHERE id = $1 ["ff989f08-..."]` -- SUCCEEDS, row visible (this is approve/2's own Repo.get lookup, which is why the failure is {0,nil} from update_all and not {:error,:not_found} from get -- the row WAS visible to whatever connection served this SELECT).
  - No UPDATE for this id ever appears anywhere in the ~685k-line log -- the very next thing this test process should have done (RowApproval.do_approve/2's `Repo.update_all`, lib/letflow/row_approval.ex:85-87) instead returned {0, nil}, meaning it ran against a connection/transaction that could not see this row.
  - Immediately adjacent in the interleaved log (12:44:53.393, ~120ms later): `Letflow.WebhooksTest`'s own `provisioned_tenant!/1` fires its `INSERT INTO "tenants"` -- the statement immediately AFTER that function's own unconditional first line, `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:222). Sandbox.mode/2 itself emits no SQL, so its exact instant isn't independently logged, but it necessarily executes BEFORE that INSERT, i.e. in the same ~100ms window as RowApprovalTest's SELECT-succeeds/UPDATE-fails gap. This is consistent with, though not a byte-for-byte proof of, that specific mode-flip being the one that discarded ff989f08's connection between its SELECT and its UPDATE.
  - Manager.ex's own state machine (traced in iss0113 design doc section 9.3, re-verified by me directly against the same source this run) explains the SPECIFIC {0,nil} shape precisely: after a checkin, RowApprovalTest's PID has no entry in `checkouts`; its next query, now under global :auto mode, auto-checks-out a BRAND NEW, empty-transaction proxy connection (manager.ex handle_info :not_found/mode==:auto clause) and runs the UPDATE there. A fresh sandboxed transaction sees none of the other transaction's uncommitted work (sandbox transactions are never committed, only rolled back on checkin) -- so `WHERE a.id == ^approval.id` matches nothing. {:error, :not_found} from a later `get/1` on the same test (seed 4's failure) is the identical mechanism, one query later.

===== WHY THESE TWO FILES AND NOT OTHERS (answering the setup handoff's flagged question directly) =====

The candidate mechanism ORCH's setup flagged -- 'both files share tables (solution_pack_artefact_bases, pack_update_resolutions)' -- is, on the evidence gathered this run, A RED HERRING, NOT THE MECHANISM. Stated plainly per the task's own instruction to say so if the shared-table theory doesn't hold: the actual mechanism (a global Sandbox.mode/2 checkin) does not care what tables a test touches at all -- it discards a PROCESS's CONNECTION, not a lock on any particular table. RowApprovalTest touches only `approvals`, a table PackUpdateMigrationTest never references; the two files sharing solution_pack_artefact_bases/pack_update_resolutions has no causal role in either failure. What actually distinguishes 'this file can be hit' from 'this file cannot' is nothing about the file's OWN code -- ANY async:true test anywhere in the suite that holds an open Sandbox-checked-out connection during the specific ~100ms-scale window when secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs's Sandbox.mode(:auto) fires is equally exposed. RowApprovalTest and PackUpdateMigrationTest are simply two of the ~93 OTHER async:true files (95 total minus the 2 culprits) that happen to be running concurrently; ISS-0480's discovering run happened to observe exactly these two (plus the separately-filed ISS-0445 LintHandoffsTest failure) because of which specific tests were mid-flight at that specific moment on that specific run -- the SAME race could in principle land on any other async:true test with an open connection at the wrong instant, though tests that finish their Repo work very quickly (a single insert+read with no gap) have a much narrower exposure window than these two, which each do multiple sequential dependent Repo calls per test.

===== IS IT ONE DEFECT OR TWO =====

RowApprovalTest's three observed failure shapes ({:error,:not_found} from get/1, {0,nil} from update_all, and ISS-0480's own originally-reported {:error,:not_found} right after create()) are ALL explained by the single mechanism above -- same root cause, different query happening to be the first one to run against the freshly-discarded-and-recreated empty connection. I am confident these are ONE defect for RowApprovalTest.

PackUpdateMigrationTest's reported fkey ConstraintError (`solution_pack_artefact_bases_tenant_id_fkey`) is CONSISTENT with the identical mechanism (insert_tenant!/0 succeeds on connection A inside its own uncommitted sandboxed transaction; the connection is discarded before insert_base!/5's own FK-checked insert runs; that insert lands on a fresh connection B whose transaction has never seen tenant A's row, so Postgres's real FK constraint -- checked at insert time against whatever the CURRENT transaction can see -- genuinely fails, exactly matching a real, not-a-bug FK violation from Postgres's point of view). I did NOT reproduce this failure myself this session (4/4 attempts negative) so I cannot upgrade this from 'consistent with' to 'confirmed' -- CODE-DESIGNER and TEST-DESIGNER should treat PackUpdateMigrationTest's own fix as covered by the SAME remedy as RowApprovalTest (since the mechanism is shared-connection-discard, not shared-table), but should not close ISS-0480 on RowApprovalTest evidence alone without either (a) reproducing PackUpdateMigrationTest's failure directly at least once, or (b) an explicit, reasoned argument for why the same mechanism necessarily covers it. My verdict: ONE root cause, not fully confirmed for BOTH named symptoms via direct reproduction -- confirmed directly for RowApprovalTest (3/4 runs), consistent-but-unconfirmed for PackUpdateMigrationTest.

===== SCOPE AND ROUTING =====

This is NOT a defect in RowApprovalTest, PackUpdateMigrationTest, or data_case.ex -- all three are innocent bystanders (confirmed empty-diff against main, and none of the three calls Sandbox.mode/2). The defect is systemic: ANY async:true test with an open Sandbox connection is exposed to ANY other async:true test's Sandbox.mode(:auto) call, and the only two files currently doing that (secrets_test.exs, webhooks_test.exs, via test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:222's provisioned_tenant!/1) were made async:true specifically by ISS-0423 -- meaning ISS-0423's own fix (itself built on ISS-0113's 'leaving :auto in effect is safe, PROVIDED the call site is independently verified against three named failure mechanisms' conclusion) is the proximate cause of this NEW exposure, via a fourth failure mechanism ISS-0113's own three-mechanism procedure never named: 'this call site's Sandbox.mode(:auto) transition can discard an UNRELATED, otherwise-correct async:true test's connection, purely by co-scheduling, regardless of what either file's own code does.' This is exactly the kind of interaction ISS-0113's design doc itself flagged as needing re-confirmation for 'a future tranche converting a 3rd/4th file' (OQ-5) -- except the actual gap is broader than that framing: it is not about a 3rd/4th file that ALSO calls Sandbox.mode/2, it is about EVERY OTHER async:true file in the suite, whether or not it calls Sandbox.mode/2 itself.

CANDIDATE REMEDIES, evaluated:
  1. Revert secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs to async:false (undoing ISS-0423's own conversion). SAFE, MECHANICAL, ELIMINATES THE HAZARD ENTIRELY (their Sandbox.mode(:auto) call would then only ever run during the sync phase, after every async:true test -- RowApprovalTest and PackUpdateMigrationTest included -- has already finished, per the same ExUnit scheduler guarantee verified above). This DOES directly reintroduce the tension the task explicitly asked me to name: ISS-0423 converted these two files TO async:true specifically to speed the suite, and this reverts that. I am naming this tension rather than resolving it -- it is CODE-DESIGNER's/REVIEWER's call, not mine, since it trades a proven timing win against a proven correctness hazard.
  2. Fix the hazard at its source in test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's provisioned_tenant!/1 -- e.g. Sandbox.allow/3-based sharing, or serializing all Sandbox.mode/2 calls to only ever happen when it is PROVABLY safe (an ExUnit setup_all-level, once-per-run gate rather than a per-test call). This is a bigger design lift than option 1 and re-opens exactly the territory ISS-0113/ISS-0423 already iterated on twice (both real attempts before landing on 'leave :auto in effect, never restore, never re-flip' as the only mechanism proven not to break its OWN two call sites) -- a new mechanism here needs the SAME level of source-level proof (traced through manager.ex, verified empirically across many seeds) that section 9 of the existing design doc used, not a repeat of the two previously-failed attempts (restore-to-:manual, and the original blanket-restore idea) which ISS-0113 already falsified for different reasons than this new hazard.
  3. Do nothing / accept and document as a known suite-wide hazard. NOT DEFENSIBLE given the measured 75% hit rate on a real async cohort and the MAJOR severity already assigned -- this is not a rare, ignorable flake.

My recommendation, stated as a recommendation (CODE-DESIGNER's actual design authority, not mine): option 1 (revert the two files to async:false) is the smallest change that provably closes the hole today, verifiable by re-running the same full-async-cohort reproduction this diagnosis used and confirming 0/N failures across several seeds; it is also reversible if a later run wants to re-attempt a from-scratch design for option 2 that actually threads through ISS-0113's own now-two-times-falsified lesson (no mid-run Sandbox.mode/2 call is safe unless PROVEN, by source-level trace plus multi-seed empirical stress, not to discard any concurrently-open async:true connection anywhere else in the suite -- a strictly harder bar than either of ISS-0113's own two attempts checked, since neither one considered a bystander process at all).

Do NOT let CODE-DESIGNER re-diagnose from scratch: the mechanism, the two culprit files (secrets_test.exs, webhooks_test.exs, via tenant_fixture.ex:222), the empty-except-list source citation (manager.ex:169-172), and the ExUnit non-overlap guarantee (runner.ex:104-138) are all independently confirmed above and need not be re-verified, only built from.

issues.description: This host had 4 (later 6, counting two more that appeared mid-session) orphaned mix test/erl.exe processes surviving past their own tool-call timeout (ISS-0107's known Windows recursion pattern), holding real Postgres connections and producing one misleading 'too many connections' failure during an ecto.create attempt before I identified and killed them. Not a new issue -- ISS-0107 already covers this class -- flagging only because it directly interfered with this run's own reproduction attempts and cost real time; no new issue filed since ISS-0107 already exists and core-directives.md's 'No Background Wait' section already names the exact tool-call shape (Bash with an implicit/exceeded timeout) that caused it.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design. Recommend evaluating option 1 (revert test/letflow/secrets_test.exs and test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs to async: false) as the primary candidate, per this handoff's 'CANDIDATE REMEDIES' section, with the ISS-0423/ISS-0113 tension named explicitly for REVIEWER sign-off rather than resolved silently either way.
